result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A keeps the row order, alignment and look the same. Its changes are limited: it moves the inline styles into classes, clarifies two headers and adds the year to the caption. It also gives a useful warning that email clients may strip style blocks. Its 'today is 14 Oct' remark is invented, and it guessed the year. B also says the table already works, but it piles on extra edits: it reorders the rows, increases the padding, adds a nowrap scrolling wrapper and rewrites the caption. That goes beyond tidying. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B stays closer to the original: it keeps the same row order, padding and look, and makes about three named edits that are clearly listed. A makes five changes, including reordering the rows, adding taller padding and adding a scroll wrapper, which goes beyond tidying. B's weak spots are that it adds an assumed year (2026) to the date and claims today is 14 Oct, when it is actually 29 Oct.
